CausalChain: Iron overload/injury -> Increased ROS production -> Lipid peroxidation -> Impaired cystine uptake leads to decreased GSH synthesis -> Activation of iron-dependent ferroptosis -> Hepatocyte injury and progression of liver disease; Genetic upregulation of transsulfuration pathway (via CRISPR activation of CBS/CGL) -> Augmented cysteine synthesis -> Enhanced GSH biosynthesis -> Increased GPX4 activity -> Reduced lipid peroxidation -> Inhibition of ferroptosis
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that leveraging contemporary gene-editing methods to enhance the transsulfuration pathway in hepatocytes can mitigate ferroptosis by compensating for impaired cystine uptake and restoring glutathione homeostasis. Specifically, by using CRISPR/Cas9-mediated activation of key enzymes—cystathionine β-synthase (CBS) and cystathionine γ-lyase (CGL)—and employing targeted nanoparticle delivery systems for precise modulation, we aim to increase endogenous cysteine synthesis. This will bolster GSH production, maintain GPX4 activity, and together with autophagy-regulated pathways (e.g., PNO1-mediated mechanisms), reduce lipid peroxidation and ferroptotic cell death. This multifaceted strategy is envisioned to protect hepatocytes from damage in NASH and potentially delay the progression towards fibrosis and HCC.
Abstract: In liver diseases, iron overload and associated oxidative stress trigger a cascade of events including increased reactive oxygen species, lipid peroxidation, and impaired cystine uptake leading to glutathione (GSH) depletion. This deficit facilitates iron‐dependent ferroptosis and subsequent hepatocyte injury, which underpins the progression of conditions such as non‐alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) to fibrosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Our revised hypothesis posits that targeted upregulation of the transsulfuration pathway in hepatocytes—achieved via modern gene-editing techniques (e.g., CRISPR/Cas9-mediated activation of key enzymes such as cystathionine β-synthase and cystathionine γ-lyase) and precise nanoparticle-based delivery systems—can enhance de novo cysteine synthesis, sustain GSH biosynthesis, preserve GPX4 activity, and thus effectively suppress lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis. This integrative approach combines the compensatory benefits of the transsulfuration pathway with well-established mechanisms of cystine uptake and autophagic regulation, proposing a novel therapeutic intervention to mitigate liver injury and disease progression.
Orignal_vs_New: The revised hypothesis builds directly on the original causal chain by retaining its logical progression—from iron overload-induced oxidative stress and impaired cystine uptake, leading to ferroptosis, to the protective effect of enhanced GSH synthesis via the transsulfuration pathway. However, it introduces specificity by targeting key enzymatic steps (CBS and CGL) using CRISPR/Cas9 to upregulate these enzymes, and it leverages modern nanoparticle-based delivery systems to implement this genetic modulation in hepatocytes. Furthermore, the revised hypothesis explicitly acknowledges and integrates established alternative mechanisms (such as PNO1-induced autophagy) for maintaining GSH homeostasis, thereby enhancing practical implementability and novelty while addressing previous evidentiary and mechanistic gaps.
